failure_reason: 50 of 97 Pet Care leaf categories have qty:null - the great majority because Walmart's own totalItemCountDisplay is capped at '(1000+)' for high-volume categories (proven unreliable/inflated beyond that cap by the prior Home-Decor pass for this same site), plus 2 categories (Training Dog Treats, Bird Perches) that hit an isolated HTTP 429 on that single request. No qty was estimated or guessed for any of these; each is flagged for manual review instead.
notes: Scoped to Walmart's dedicated Pet department hub (https://www.walmart.com/cp/pets/5440), reached via direct HTTP fetch (no WAF/block encountered on any request except two isolated HTTP 429s on individual category URLs - all other ~96 requests to walmart.com returned 200, so those two are treated as transient rate-limit blips, not a host block, per brief section 1). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (checked directly, same as prior Home-Decor pass note). Site structure discovered via the embedded __NEXT_DATA__ CategoryTopNav module on the Pet hub page, which exposes the full Dog/Cat/Fish/Bird/Small Pet/Reptile/Farm Animal mega-menu as clean JSON (category -> subCategoryGroup), used instead of scraping rendered HTML nav. This mirrors the exact totalItemCount/totalItemCountDisplay methodology validated in the prior Home-Decor pass for this same company (SR194 archive c226): an exact (non-capped) totalItemCountDisplay was accepted as qty; any '(1000+)' capped display was treated as unreliable/inflated at Walmart's scale and set to null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag, since that prior pass proved capped counts are internally inconsistent across parent/child scopes on this site. Boundary calls: Cat Litter & Accessories kept in full (Tier 1 hygiene & waste, explicit in the brief). All *_Food, *_Treats, and farm-animal *_Feed categories were kept (not dropped) but flagged MANUAL REVIEW: PET CONSUMABLE per the brief's open policy gap. Dog/Cat Health & Wellness and Flea & Tick were kept but flagged MANUAL REVIEW: PET MEDICAL / VETERINARY CATEGORY per the brief's other open policy gap. The 'Farm Animal' branch (Cattle, Chicken Coops/Supplies, Horse Shampoo) sits under Walmart's own Pets department but is agricultural/livestock in nature rather than companion-pet care, so those non-feed leaves were kept but flagged MANUAL REVIEW: FARM/LIVESTOCK CATEGORY for a human boundary call. Species hub pages under 'All Small Pets' (Ferrets, Rats, Chinchillas, Gerbils) and 'Chicken Supplies' mix food+bedding+cages+toys under one browse node rather than a single product type, so they were kept but flagged as mixed-content. Fish Tanks/Filters/Heating/Decoration and Bird Aviaries/Perches, Terrariums, Reptile Foggers/Heating Lamps, and all *_Cages/_Bedding nodes were included as Tier 1 Housing & containment / habitat equipment analogs. Excluded/dropped: generic marketing nav items on every mega-menu column (All Pet Supplies, Pet Deals, Shop by Brand, New Arrivals, Walmart Business - not real categories per brief section 4), 'Pet Services' (grooming/vet appointment booking, not a product category), 'Pet Insurance' and 'Pet Pharmacy' (financial/medical services, not product listings), and Fish Food Treats (duplicate of the Fish Food parent listing URL, no distinct facet - noted below). Pet Tech appeared identically under both Dog and Cat nav columns (same URL) and was merged into one row per the brief's same-URL-merge rule. Did not attempt full site search or sitemap enumeration since the Pet hub's own mega-menu already gave a complete, site-declared category tree (absence proof via real navigation, not search). This is PLP/category-level extraction only; no individual product pages were opened. Cat > Cat Supplies > Pet Tech: same URL/listing as Dog > Dog Supplies > Pet Tech (site reuses one 'All Pet Smart Tech' node across Dog and Cat nav) - merged into single row under Dog, not duplicated.; Fish > Fish Food > Fish Food Treats: dropped, same underlying listing URL as parent 'Fish Food' (site's own duplicate nav entry, no distinct facet).. Of 97 leaf (non-group) rows, 50 carry qty:null (capped '(1000+)' counts, 2 HTTP-429 misses, or policy-flagged categories with an otherwise-capped count) - status set to 'partial' given this large null fraction, consistent with the project's convention for large general marketplaces (Etsy US / QVC / Noon UAE / this same company's prior Home-Decor pass).
